spaces.label: Spaces
spaces.createDescription: Creates the space (a namespace labeled kite.application/space) on every selected cluster and applies the entered resource quota there; failed clusters keep the succeeded ones and can be retried.
spaces.clusterRequired: Select at least one target cluster.
spaces.invalidName: Name must be a lowercase DNS label: a-z, 0-9 and "-", at most 63 characters.
spaces.quotaLocked: This space already exists on the cluster; edit its quota in space settings.
spaces.quotaRequired: Enter a CPU (core) and memory (GiB) quota greater than 0 for every selected cluster.
spaces.createPartial: Space {{name}} created on {{succeeded}}; failed on {{failed}} (succeeded clusters are kept)
spaces.lockedOnWorkflowEditor: Space is locked while editing a workflow (it follows the workflow’s binding)

status.spaceUnlinkedNote: Space unlinked: the namespace no longer belongs to this space

list.name: Name
list.deleteDescription: The application is not deployed; only its definition in the database will be deleted.
list.deleteBlocked: This application has cluster configs (deployed or drifted) — offline them first. Deletion also cleans up kept offline configs and revisions.
list.refreshStatusHint: Re-run the drift check for every config on this page (results are persisted for the list aggregation)
list.aggregationHint: Status is a persisted snapshot of the latest check; refresh statuses to update it

detail.undeployedTitle: Not bound to any cluster yet
detail.undeployedHint: The first publish happens here: pick a target cluster and confirm the publish to deploy.
detail.podRestarted: Pod {{pod}} is restarting (recreated by its controller)
detail.forceDeleteHint: Delete the pod immediately (grace period 0), for pods stuck in Terminating
detail.podForceDeleted: Pod {{pod}} force deleted; the controller will recreate it
detail.offlinedTitle: Never successfully published on this cluster
detail.offlinedHint: The first publish did not succeed or the config was offlined; republishing creates the cluster resources from the current DB-side config.
detail.podUsageHint: Top: live usage; bottom: requests / limits
detail.controllerSpecHint: Pod template resource limits of the workload (all containers)
detail.controllerImageHint: Pod template image of the workload
detail.unauthorized: No permission to read this section
detail.unlinkedHint: This config's namespace no longer belongs to the space, so the runtime view is hidden; the stored config can still be viewed as YAML or copied to another cluster.
detail.docMissingInCluster: Pending publish: this document does not exist in the cluster yet
detail.docMissingInManifests: Only in the cluster; the DB config does not track it
detail.pathsTruncated: Too many changed paths, list truncated
detail.applySelectionHint: Cluster-side picks adopt the live cluster value into the DB config; DB-side picks keep the stored value. Nothing to apply while the cluster count is 0.
detail.applyConfirmBody: Cluster side ({{cluster}} paths): the live cluster value is adopted into the DB config. DB side ({{db}} paths): the stored value stays unchanged.
detail.resolveApplied: Selection applied; the DB config now carries the adopted cluster values
detail.syncedBanner: Config is consistent with the cluster, no drift.
detail.podNotFound: Pod not found or reclaimed — it may have been rescheduled.
detail.relatedWorkflowsEmpty: No workflow deploys this app yet. Create one to build and deploy it.

deploy.title: Publish {{namespace}} / {{name}} to {{cluster}}?
deploy.targetClusterHint: Filtered by connectivity; confirming the publish deploys the app to this cluster.
deploy.copyCreateHint: Lists online clusters not bound by this app yet; confirming deep-copies {{source}}'s config as the initial config.
deploy.imageHint: Changing the image publishes it: the change is saved to the DB config first, then pushed with this publish
deploy.pullCredentialHint: On every publish, kite upserts a managed dockerconfigjson secret (kite-pull-<credential>) in the target namespace from the credential's registry entries and references it on the workload automatically; YAML-edited configs keep the manual contract — reference imagePullSecrets yourself there.
deploy.createModeHint: Pick a target cluster — the server-side dry-run then renders the resources to create in memory and validates them.
deploy.createModeDocs: First publish · creates {{count}} resources (create mode: never overwrites existing objects)
deploy.noChanges: DB config matches the cluster — change the image, edit the config, or modify other settings to publish.
deploy.dryRunOkCreate: Create mode: only creates, never overwrites · server-side dry-run passed
deploy.anchorHint: After a successful publish the objects are read back and the consistency anchor is updated.
deploy.saveOnlyHint: Persist as a DB revision without publishing to the cluster; the pull credential takes effect with the publish
deploy.savedNotPublished: Saved as pending changes — not published to the cluster yet
deploy.previewStale: Cluster state changed; the preview has been reloaded
deploy.success: Published to {{cluster}}; anchor read back from the cluster
deploy.viewDocDiff: Click to view the YAML diff
deploy.unchangedDocs: {{count}} more documents re-applied without content changes

offline.title: Offline {{name}} on {{cluster}}?
offline.description: This deletes the Deployment / Service / Ingress and other resources on that cluster, plus this cluster's config with its full revision chain — irreversibly. If the app then has no config left, deploying again starts from the initial definition.
offline.deleteAppHint: Delete the application from the list instead — all clusters must be offline first.
offline.purged: Offline complete on {{cluster}}; cluster resources, the config and its revisions are deleted
offline.clusterGone: Cluster {{cluster}} no longer exists; config taken offline without cluster cleanup
offline.partialFailure: Some cluster deletions failed; the config is kept for retry

history.title: Revisions · {{namespace}} / {{name}} · {{cluster}}
history.rollbackHint: View the diff of this revision against the current config, then confirm to roll back and publish
history.rollbackConflict: The config was modified concurrently; refresh and retry
history.selectHint: Select any two revisions to compare. Rollback opens a diff against the current config — confirm inside to write back and publish.
history.rolledBack: Rolled back to rev {{rev}} and published
history.rollbackSelfHint: This is the current revision — nothing to roll back
history.rollbackIdentical: The target revision is identical to the current config — nothing to roll back.

editors.requestsFollowHint: Requests default to an overcommitted profile — CPU at half the limit, memory equal to the limit — and can be overridden individually
editors.requestExceedsCpu: CPU request must not exceed the limit
editors.requestExceedsMemory: Memory request must not exceed the limit

wizard.appNameHint: The space is fixed to the sidebar's current space (read-only) — switch it in the sidebar first if needed; the name takes lowercase letters/digits/dashes and cannot change after creation.
wizard.spaceRequired: Pick a space in the sidebar first — applications are always created inside a space.
wizard.noSpacesHint: A space is a cluster namespace labeled kite.application/space=true. Create a space first, then come back to create the application.
wizard.workloadTypeLocked: Type is locked once deployed: take the app offline, then change it and republish.
wizard.invalidName: Name must be a lowercase DNS label (a-z, 0-9, '-') of at most 63 characters.
wizard.nameExists: An application with this name already exists in this space.
wizard.previewPlaceholderHint: Fill in the application name in step 1 (Basic Info) to render the preview and create the app.
wizard.limitsRequired: CPU and memory limits are required
wizard.envHint: Referenced variables (Secret / ConfigMap refs, envFrom) are maintained in YAML mode (step 6).
wizard.batchPastePlaceholder:
KEY=VALUE
One per line — paste .env content directly
wizard.batchPasteHint: Blank lines and # comments ignored; same-name keys overwritten
wizard.invalidYaml: Invalid YAML — please check the syntax
wizard.switchToYaml: Switch to YAML mode (edit full manifests)
wizard.yamlReadOnlyHint: After creation, full manifests can be edited in YAML mode from the cluster config's wizard.
wizard.yamlEditableHint: Edits cover the full multi-document manifests (--- separated); the form view is refilled from known fields, unknown fields are preserved.
wizard.previewEmpty: Fill in the app name to render a preview
wizard.extraYaml: Advanced · ExtraYAML (extra multi-docs applied with every publish)
wizard.extraYamlPlaceholder:
# e.g. mount a ConfigMap, PVC, HPA...
# apiVersion: v1
# kind: ConfigMap
# metadata:
#   name: my-app-config
# data:
#   app.properties: |
#     key=value
wizard.extraYamlHint: Extra docs are applied with every publish; advanced fields not covered by the form are maintained in YAML mode.
wizard.targetClusterHint: The app is published to the selected cluster on creation: its definition is rendered as that cluster's initial config, created and published on confirm.
wizard.clusterRequired: Select a target cluster — the app is published there on creation.
wizard.draftNoCluster: The app is not bound to a cluster yet
wizard.draftNoClusterHint: Save the draft, then start the first publish from the detail page.
wizard.configFilesHint: A mount directory is a directory inside the container; every config file is mounted as a concrete file under it (e.g. /etc/my-app/app.conf), covering only that file without hiding the rest of the directory. The mount path is picked from the directories via dropdown when adding/editing files.
wizard.noMountPoints: No mount directories yet — default /etc/<app> is used when files exist
wizard.mountPointInvalid: Must be an absolute path starting with /
wizard.fullPath: Full file path inside the container
wizard.configFilesEmptyHint: No config files needed? Just continue to the next step.
wizard.configFilesAdvancedHint: Shared ConfigMaps/Secrets, envFrom, directory mounts and other advanced usages go through YAML mode / ExtraYAML after saving.
wizard.secretMarker: Sensitive (stored in the Secret; masked in views and audit) — rendered as <app>-secret, default <app>-config for {{app}}
wizard.portsHint: Port names are auto-generated (e.g. tcp_80) — no need to fill them. "＋ External host" configures external access (renders an Ingress rule); without it the port is cluster-internal only (Service).

spaceQuota.title: Resource Quotas · {{name}}
spaceQuota.description: Per-cluster quota of this space, enforced by the kite-managed ResourceQuota in the space's namespace (cpu / memory and limits.cpu / limits.memory share the same value).
spaceQuota.overCapacity: Quota exceeds the cluster's allocatable capacity
spaceQuota.overCapacityHint: Exceeds the cluster's allocatable {{limit}}. Oversubscription is allowed on shared clusters, but this is usually a typo.
spaceQuota.empty: This space has no namespace on any known cluster yet.
spaceQuota.unlinkHint: Removes the space marker from namespace {{space}} on cluster {{cluster}} only; the namespace and its workloads are not deleted and the quota object stays. Re-adopt the space any time from the create dialog.
spaceQuota.unlinked: Cluster {{cluster}} is no longer a space
spaceQuota.editHint: Applies the kite-managed ResourceQuota in this space's namespace on {{cluster}}. The request is idempotent — retrying after a failure is safe.
spaceQuota.saveFailed: Failed to save the quota on {{cluster}}: {{error}}

editors.imageHint: Specify the container image including tag (e.g., nginx:1.21, node:16-alpine)
editors.pullHintIfNotPresent: Pull image only if not present locally
editors.pullHintNever: Never pull, use local image only
